summary:
Webhook sender retries are complete: transport and retryable server failures retry with capped exponential backoff, while 4xx errors fail immediately; handler retries remain prohibited. All 44 tests pass, Ruff passes, and the diff is clean.

Search rebuild performance was optimized using tenant-scoped invoice queries and concurrent, ordered embedding batches of 100. A 5,000-document dry run improved from 8.42s to 1.19s. Search rebuilder/index tests pass (33), though the broader indexing baseline still has 2 failures involving stale invoice descriptions. The management command now shares its `EmbeddingClient`; one tenant migration helper may still use the old per-document path.

Elasticsearch `orders_v1` and `orders_v2` each contain 18,432 documents; alias/switchover remains.

Immediate priority remains fixing `ledgerly/dunning/scheduler.py`, which emails reminders to paid customers. Also treat `billing_v3` as active; never write to frozen `billing_v1`.

Resolved the usage-consumer retention leak by copying batches before extending pending events and removing `BillingWorker._last_batch`. A 5-event isolation regression was added; all worker tests pass, the full suite reports 118 passed/7 skipped, and a 5,000-batch reproduction settled at 2.1 MiB retained with zero pending events. Treat fields ending in `_secret`, `_token`, or `_fingerprint` as restricted and pass them only via `safe_customer_context`; webhook-handler retries remain ruled out because they duplicated customer emails.

The original router-splitting goal in `ledgerly/api/routes.py` remains untouched. The Elasticsearch alias procedure has only completed health checking; the cluster is yellow, and steps 2–8 remain. New licensing dependencies must be exactly pinned in `requirements/license-tools.txt`.
